- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 10–15 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 80+ values), then corrects with a downward bias later.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion or lagged response to recent price action.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the middle of the horizon (days 15–25), often peaking before true price stabilizes.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices (e.g., >82).
- When history contains a strong upward trend, model overreacts with exaggerated peaks; when trend is flat or declining, model underreacts.
- Forecasts show diminishing sensitivity to recent history as horizon extends — later days are less responsive to recent spikes.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after high peaks; often misses the “drop-off” phase after a spike.
- True outcomes often show a “reversion to mean” pattern after initial spikes, while model continues to trend upward.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of downward corrections, especially after a price spike followed by a correction.
